needsYou.description: Open, not a draft, and not yet handled by you.

testsTotal.description: Check runs of the head commit (a re-run replaces the earlier run of the same name).

testsPassed.description: Of those, completed with success, neutral or skipped.

testsFailed.description: Of those, completed with any other conclusion.

PullCounts.description: Size of each inbox tab, over every repo of the project.

patch.description: GitHub's unified diff; null for binary files and diffs that are too large.

checks.description: CI check runs of the head commit, failures first.

checksState.description: `none` when no check run is stored (not synced, or the repo has no CI).

conclusion.description: GitHub's: success, failure, neutral, cancelled, skipped, timed_out, action_required, stale; null until completed.

headSha.description: The commit the review was left on.

stage.description: queued, reading, reviewing, refuting, done or failed.

walkthrough.description: Markdown, set once the review succeeded.

backend.description: Which Claude ran it: the owner's subscription, the requester's own key, or the server's key.

findings.description: Findings a refuter confirmed, most severe first.

dropped.description: Findings the refuters could not confirm, left out.

spec.description: Path of the spec the finding breaks, when it names one.

root.description: Folder holding the `spec` folder, '' at the top of the repo.

area.description: Folders between `spec/` and the file, '' when flat.

tested.description: Requirements with at least one test anchored to them or to their step.

devpage.description: The spec as devpage server renders it, on this origin; null while devpage is off or has not published it.

SpecModel.description: Null when the file has errors; see diagnostics.

source.description: The whole spec file as edited.

summary.description: One line per change, for the pull request.

path.description: Under a `spec/` folder; the file name is the flow id.

tools.description: Read tools called for this reply, such as `pulls.list(filter=needs)`.

ran.description: Indexes of `actions` the user already ran.

changes.description: What the coordinator changed on the board, in words, such as `Added a flowchart`.

board.description: The coordinator's changes to the whiteboard the user was on, already applied; null when it changed nothing.

changes.description: What changed, by id, such as `Added checkout.pay/r3`.

skipped.description: Changes the coordinator asked for that could not be made, and why.

requirements.description: The coordinator's changes to the requirements set the user was on, already applied; null when it changed nothing.

path.description: For `open`: the app route to go to, such as /pr/<id>.

boardId.description: For `draft_requirements`: the whiteboard to draft from.

CoordinatorAction.description: Something the coordinator proposes. Nothing runs until the user clicks it.

CoordinatorBoard.description: The whiteboard after the coordinator's change (or its undo).

ids.description: Every id this set has issued, in order. An id is never reused.

path.description: Where the flow goes in a repo as a spec.

source.description: The flow as a spec file.

allOf.description: Null when the flow has errors; see diagnostics.

of.description: The step or requirement id it illustrates, null for the whole set.

CoordinatorScreen.description: What the user is looking at.

get.description: `filter` is the inbox tab: `needs` (open, not a draft, not yet handled by you), `open`, `merged`, or `all` (default). `repo` (`owner/name`) narrows the list to one repo; `counts` always covers every repo. Needs-you PRs come first, then the most recently updated.

post.summary: Approve a pull request or request changes (owner only)
post.description: Leaves a review on GitHub as the App, on the PR's current head commit, and records it. An approval takes the PR out of `needs` until its head moves. `request_changes` needs a `body`.

post.summary: Merge a pull request on GitHub (owner only)
post.description: Merges the PR at the head commit spectrace last saw (`squash` unless `method` says otherwise). GitHub refuses when the PR is not mergeable or its head has moved; that comes back as 409 and a sync will refresh it.

post.description: Runs the action through the same API as the buttons on each page: start the Reviewer agent (`review_pull`), approve, merge, pull from GitHub, re-index. `open` is navigation and runs in the browser. The outcome is added to the conversation.

post.description: Puts the board or the set back as it was before this reply changed it. Only while nobody changed it since; otherwise 409.

post.summary: Draft requirements from a whiteboard and your conversation with the coordinator
post.description: Claude turns the board and the discussion into flows in the spec format (steps and WHEN/SHALL requirements with stable ids) and views of those ids: screen mockups, other diagrams and notes. Each flow is checked by the spec parser; a flow that does not parse gets one repair round, and keeps its diagnostics if it still fails.
